messages:
samira: heads up — secret-scan v2.2 flagged an AWS session token inside an archived branch tarball in CI cache :rotating_light:
sec-bot: automated-detection: repo=infra/service-x, path=/build-cache/archives/feat-noise/old-proto.tar.gz, pattern=AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, confidence=0.82
matt: which branch and when did the archive get uploaded? can we assume creds are short-lived sts tokens or long-lived keys?
samira: branch=feat/noise (archived). artifact uploaded ~2024-11-02 per build metadata. token looks like STS-style session token (starts with AQoDYXdz...), so likely temporary but still actionable. scan showed no AccessKeyId nearby in the blob.
jen-devops: for STS tokens we can't "revoke" the token directly. we should: 1) check CloudTrail for usage, 2) rotate any long-lived keys associated with the role, 3) delete artifact from storage and purge caches, 4) block artifact access and add artifact-read RBAC. i'll take 2+3.
elaine: kicking off CloudTrail query for the time window. running: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --start-time 2024-11-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-11-05T00:00:00Z --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRole``` will filter assume-role events to find suspicious sessions.
josh: created SEC ticket SEC-472 and added initial notes + urgency=high. PR created to sanitize repo history and remove archive references: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1293 (WIP).
samira: removed the tarball from S3 and invalidated the artefact cache: ```aws s3 rm s3://ci-artifacts/service-x/archives/feat-noise/old-proto.tar.gz && curl -X PURGE https://cache.internal/ci/service-x/feat-noise``` verified MD5 mismatch no longer present.
jen-devops: rotated service principal long-lived keys (service-x-deploy role). commands used (summary): ```aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIA... --status Inactive``` then created new key and updated KMS-encrypted secrets in the secrets manager. also enabled object-level KMS envelope encryption on the artifacts bucket.
matt: thanks. two follow-ups: (1) limit read permission on ci caches so only build-runner-service principal + SRE debugging ACLs can read; (2) add a failsafe alert so secret-scan findings in artifact storage create paging incidents.
elaine: added CloudTrail saved query and SIEM rule (Splunk) to alert on s3:GetObject for ci-artifacts/* by non-build-runner principals. also added audit logging for who purged artifacts.
samira: quick notes for post-incident: - incident type: secret in archived CI artifact - severity: medium (no confirmed exfiltration) - containment: artifact removed, cache invalidated, keys rotated - detection: automated secret-scan + manual validation - next actions: retro, RBAC change, audit log forwarding, KMS enforced on artifacts.
josh: tagging product and legal per policy; created a short comms blurb for impacted teams. will post in #general after legal OK.
jen-devops: opened infra PR to enforce KMS on ci-artifacts bucket + tightened IAM on cache read: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1296 (reviewers: matt, elaine)
matt: assign owners and due dates in SEC-472. deadline: 2024-12-01 for RBAC + KMS enforcement.
sec-bot: incident-update: SEC-472 status=contained, remediation=partial, followups=open [SEC-472-1: RBAC tighten, SEC-472-2: SIEM rule, SEC-472-3: retro & docs]. closing thread once PRs merged and SIEM rule validated. :thumbsup:
